sections.sectionTitle: Paper 1: West Africa and the Wider World (Earliest Times to 2000)

topics.title: Historiography, Trade, Religions, and Early Contact

subtopics.content: Historiography, sources of history, ICT in historical studies, Trans-Saharan trade, spread of Islam, European contact, and Trans-Atlantic slave trade
subtopics.objective: Understand historical methods, sources, and ICT prospects; examine Trans-Saharan trade origins and impacts; analyze the introduction and spread of Islam; evaluate European arrival, trade, and Trans-Atlantic slave trade origins, organization, and suppression.

topics.title: Missionary Activities, Partition, Colonialism, and Post-Independence International Relations

subtopics.content: Christian missions, Scramble and Partition of Africa, patterns of colonial rule, World Wars, post-independence political/economic issues, military rule, and international organizations (UN, AU, ECOWAS)
subtopics.objective: Assess Christian missionary impact; analyze the Scramble for Africa, colonial conquest, and African resistance; evaluate colonial administration systems and economic underdevelopment; analyze post-independence problems including military coups and boundary disputes; examine West African participation in UNO, AU, and ECOWAS.

subtopics.content: Country-specific pre-colonial ethnic origins and centralized/non-centralized states, 19th-century political developments/wars, colonial administration/decolonization, and post-independence political history up to 2000
subtopics.objective: Detail pre-colonial social, political, and economic organizations for candidate's home country (The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, or Sierra Leone); analyze 19th-century transformations (jihadist movements, state expansion, missionary work, resistance); evaluate colonial governance (Indirect Rule, Crown Colony), economic developments, decolonization, and post-independence political eras up to 2000.
